title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Green Bay, WI: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Green Bay paper mill, shipyard, fire apparatus and bridge welding inspectors: Part C code choice, Part B travel and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Green Bay: Six Days for Northeast Wisconsin Paper Mill, Shipyard, Vehicle and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Northeast Wisconsin welds three very different kinds of product. Along the Fox River, paper mills run long trains of steam-heated rolls, pressure vessels and pipe that need welding repairs every time a machine comes down. On the bay and on the Menominee River, shipyards build and repair steel vessels. Inland, in the Fox Valley, vehicle builders weld fire apparatus bodies and chassis parts. A welding inspector in Green Bay can spend a career in any one of those worlds, and each of them values an inspector who can read a standard and apply it without guesswork.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day preparation course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, written for Green Bay and Fox Valley welders, shipfitters, millwrights, QC staff, NDT technicians and engineers. The American Welding Society administers the examination and issues the certification, and you apply to AWS as an individual who meets its education, experience and vision rules in your own right. Atlantis is not AWS-approved or AWS-endorsed and has never seen examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Green Bay. You can follow the six days online at your own pace, have them delivered at your employer's mill, yard or plant for a group, or take them one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Day-by-day topics are listed on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Paper mills on the Fox River

Paper remains central to Green Bay industry. Georgia-Pacific's Broadway mill started production on its eighth paper machine in June 2024, the first new machine at the site in more than three decades, along with new converting lines and more than 600,000 square feet of added space for retail products such as Brawny paper towels. A machine like that is surrounded by welded steel: steam-heated dryer cylinders and other pressure equipment, steam and condensate piping, stock tanks, structural supports and walkways.

Mill welding is mostly maintenance and capital project work, and most of it happens in short windows. During an outage, contractors and the mill's own maintenance crews cut out worn sections, weld in new spool pieces, repair supports and replace platforms, all under pressure to restart on time. That is where an inspector earns trust: checking that a repair follows the approved procedure, that preheat and interpass limits are respected on thick nozzles, that fillet sizes and weld profiles meet the drawing and that the paperwork is complete before the line is released. Pressure piping and steam systems in a mill are usually built and repaired to ASME rules, so mill inspectors tend to lean toward the ASME option for Part C.

Mills also use a lot of stainless steel where stock, white water and process chemicals would corrode carbon steel. That brings purge practice on pipe root passes, heat tint, filler selection and dissimilar-metal joints between stainless and carbon steel into the inspector's day. None of it is exotic, but each item needs a procedure that covers it and an inspector who checks that the welder followed that procedure rather than habit.

Shipyards on the bay and the Menominee

Fincantieri Marine Group operates shipyards in Marinette and Sturgeon Bay and a facility in Green Bay. In late 2025 the Navy cancelled the last four Constellation-class frigates planned for Fincantieri Marinette Marine, where work on the first two continued, and in February 2026 the yard was picked to build Medium Landing Ships for the Marine Corps. In April 2026 the Navy awarded it a contract for long-lead material and planning for the first four McClung-class ships, which are based on Damen's LST-100 tank landing ship design, and USNI News reported that construction could start by the end of that year. In September 2025 the company said it had hired about 400 people at Marinette and about 200 at Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding in Sturgeon Bay since February of that year.

The most recent news points at the welding itself. In October 2026 Fox 11 reported that Landing Ship Medium work was driving upgrades at the company's Marinette, Sturgeon Bay and Green Bay facilities, including robotic welding systems and advanced cutting and forming equipment, with workers to be trained to run them. Navy shipbuilding contracts name the fabrication, welding and inspection requirements each ship is built to, and the yard qualifies its inspectors to them. A CWI does not replace those qualifications. What it gives a shipyard QC hand is a recognized, portable grounding in processes, symbols, procedure and welder qualification, metallurgy and discontinuities, which makes the contract documents far easier to learn and apply.

Fire apparatus and vehicle structures in the Fox Valley

Pierce Manufacturing builds fire apparatus on its Appleton campus. In December 2025 it described new equipment there that included automated rail welding systems it said cut welding time by up to two-thirds, handheld laser welding that causes minimal warpage, a laser cutter able to cut beveled edges in steel up to two inches thick, and automated bending. Fire apparatus combine steel chassis members with bodies and compartments that are often aluminum or stainless, so an inspector in a vehicle plant may move between heavy steel fillet welds and thin sheet in the same shift.

Aluminum welding has its own Part C book, AWS D1.2, and its own inspection habits: watching for porosity and lack of fusion, checking that heat input has not distorted thin panels, and confirming filler alloy and cleaning steps. A candidate whose job is mainly aluminum vehicle structures should compare D1.2 with D1.1 before choosing.

Laser welding raises its own questions. A handheld laser weld is narrow and distorts the part very little, but it leaves little visible margin for error, so the inspector looks closely for undercut, underfill, cracks at the start and stop, and signs of incomplete fusion at the root. Visual acceptance is only as good as the criteria written for that joint, and the procedure has to be qualified to whatever specification the customer invokes.

When a robot does the welding

Robotic and automated welding are spreading through every one of these sectors, from shipyard panel lines to truck frame cells. Automation changes what an inspector looks at more than it reduces the work. Instead of watching every arc, the inspector checks the first parts off a new program, verifies that fixtures and fit-up are holding tolerance, samples production at an agreed rate, reviews parameter records and repeats the first-part check whenever a program, a wire, a gas supply or a fixture changes. A single bad setting on a robot repeats itself on every part until someone notices, which makes disciplined sampling and good records more valuable, not less. The fundamentals in Part A, especially process variables and the causes of discontinuities, are exactly what that kind of judgement rests on.

Matching Part C to Northeast Wisconsin work

AWS lets each candidate pick the book for Part C, an open-book test of 50 to 65 questions. The editions below are the ones on the AWS CWI page in November 2026.

Mill maintenance, boiler and steam piping, process piping: the ASME package, Section IX (2023) with B31.1 and B31.3 (2024 editions). Procedure and welder qualification records in a mill are written around Section IX.

Shipyard structural work and general steel fabrication: AWS D1.1, 2020 edition. No naval or classification-society document is on the list, and D1.1 is the closest general structural code.

Aluminum vehicle bodies, enclosures and marine superstructure parts: AWS D1.2, 2014 edition.

Highway bridge fabrication and repair: AWS D1.5, 2020 edition including Clause 12, written for bridge steel and fracture-critical members.

Gas pipeline construction and maintenance crews: API 1104, 22nd edition.

Code and table numbers move between editions, so study the edition AWS names, even when the copy at work is newer. Reading: ASME Section IX, ASME B31.1, AWS D1.1 and AWS D1.5.

NWTC and the AWS Fox Valley Section

Northeast Wisconsin Technical College offers its Welding technical diploma at its Green Bay and Marinette campuses, with day, evening and full-time options. The program is laid out as two semesters totaling 32 credits, taught in eight-week blocks, and covers shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, gas tungsten arc, flux cored arc, submerged arc and metal core welding, with courses in Blueprint Reading for Welders, Weld Symbols and Metallurgy, with pipe welding covered inside the gas metal arc and flux cored courses. NWTC also runs a Metal Fabrication technical diploma and an employment and certification testing service. Graduates of a diploma like this normally apply under the trade or vocational line of the AWS experience table, though AWS makes the final call.

For section activity, the AWS Fox Valley Section belongs to District 12; its 2025 officers' meetings were held in Greenville, Wisconsin, and in autumn 2026 its page listed a November plant tour of Merrill Steel. The section finder on aws.org shows which section serves your ZIP code and when its next technical meeting is, and section meetings are one of the easier places to find a working CWI willing to talk through the exam.

Milwaukee, Chicago or Detroit for Part B

Parts A and C are computer-based tests taken at a Prometric test center once AWS has accepted your application. Part B, the practical, is held at AWS seminar locations, usually on the weekend after a three-day Part B seminar that runs Wednesday to Friday at the same location. Milwaukee is the Wisconsin city on the AWS list of CWI training locations, and Chicago and Detroit are the other sites a Green Bay candidate is likely to consider. AWS asks for US applications six weeks before a Part B date, and each part requires a minimum score of 72 percent, so plan the trip, the overnight stay and a possible retake into your calendar.

Part B has 46 questions built around hands-on tasks with AWS-supplied specimens, tools and documents, including applying a procedure specification and its qualification record. Practise with a fillet gauge, a bridge cam gauge and a pit gauge on real welds until reading them is quick and repeatable. To budget the trip, use the CWI exam cost calculator.

Building an experience record AWS can verify

AWS trades formal education against documented welding-related experience. Its CWI page lists one year for a bachelor's degree or higher in welding engineering or technology, two for an associate degree or higher in welding or a related engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, three for engineering or technical courses applicable to a welding bachelor's degree, four for completed trade or vocational courses, five for a high school diploma or equivalent, nine for eighth-grade schooling and twelve for less.

Green Bay careers tend to be spread across employers: a few years with a mill contractor, a spell at a shipyard, a move to a truck plant. That makes the record harder to assemble, not weaker. For every employer, write down the dates, the processes and materials, the codes or specifications you worked to, any inspection, documentation or qualification-test duties, and a person who can confirm them. Shipyard welders who moved into QC can often point to their welder qualification test records, which help show the welding-related side of the job. Ask for confirmation while those people are still easy to reach; a supervisor who retires or a contractor that closes can leave a gap that takes months to fill. AWS also requires you to pass its vision test, recorded on the AWS visual acuity form, close enough to the exam that the result is current. See the CWI requirements guide for how AWS reads an application.

Six days around mill outages and yard schedules

Outages and launch schedules make fixed class times hard for many Green Bay candidates, which is why the online format has no scheduled sessions. You work through the material on your own calendar and send questions to the instructor, who answers in writing. A workable plan is to finish the fundamentals and welding symbols before applying, use the AWS review period for the code book, and keep the timed practice papers for the last fortnight before Part A, avoiding a planned outage if you can. The one-to-one format suits a candidate who wants the six days compressed into time off between outages, or who needs focused work on one weak part.

A group course at a mill, yard or plant

A mill, shipyard supplier or vehicle plant with several candidates can have the six days delivered on site. The group practises on its own weld samples with its own gauges, and the code sessions can follow the book most of the group will take, whether that is the ASME package for a mill or D1.1 for a fabrication shop. Employers often time the course before a capital project, a new contract or a customer audit, so the credential is in place when it is needed. AWS still deals with every candidate separately, so each one files an individual application with experience evidence and a vision record.

After the CWI

A CWI stays valid for nine years under AWS rules, and AWS expects renewal applications at the three-year and six-year marks. At nine years the AWS options include retaking Part B, documenting 80 professional development hours, the Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential, an endorsement exam passed before the ninth year, the Senior CWI exams or the nine-year course. Many Northeast Wisconsin inspectors also add NDT methods, which an employer certifies under its written practice. Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including UT Level 2 for thickness and weld work in mills and yards, MT Level 2, PT Level 2 for aluminum and stainless, and VT Level 2. Mill inspectors who later move toward pressure equipment programs sometimes add an API individual certification; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers those examinations and certifies inspectors.

Local pages: NDT training in Green Bay and Practical NDT simulator access from Green Bay. CWI exam prep in nearby cities: Milwaukee, Minneapolis, Chicago and Detroit.

Your Green Bay enquiry

Send the format you prefer, the number of candidates, the Part C book each expects to choose and the season they want to sit the exam. For an on-site group, list the outage or production weeks the course should avoid. If an experience record has gaps between employers, describe them and we will say what to confirm with AWS first. Every format is priced on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Green Bay?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Green Bay. The six days run online at your own pace, at your employer's site as a group, or one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: Does a CWI qualify me to inspect welds on a Navy ship?
faq.a: Not on its own. Each naval contract names the fabrication and inspection requirements that apply, and the shipyard qualifies its inspectors to them. The CWI is a strong foundation for that qualification, not a replacement for it.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits paper mill maintenance work?
faq.a: Usually the ASME package, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because mill steam and process piping repairs are qualified and documented under ASME rules. Choose D1.1 if most of your work is structural steel.

faq.q: Where would a Green Bay candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location. Milwaukee is the Wisconsin site on the AWS list, and Chicago and Detroit are the other options most candidates from the region consider.

faq.q: I completed the NWTC Welding technical diploma. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses place you on the four-year line of the AWS table, if AWS accepts the diploma and your work as welding-related. A high school diploma alone calls for five years.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section near Green Bay?
faq.a: The AWS Fox Valley Section, part of District 12, is the nearest one we could confirm; its 2025 officers' meetings were held in Greenville, Wisconsin. The section finder on aws.org shows the section for your ZIP code.

faq.q: Can a shipyard supplier or mill contractor host the course?
faq.a: Yes. Under the corporate format the six days are delivered at your site with your own samples and gauges. Every person still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Is the course approved or endorsed by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has neither approved nor endorsed it, and Atlantis sees no AWS examination content or candidate results. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I get a quote from Green Bay?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page with the format, the number of people and the Part C book. Every format is quoted on request, and we answer within one business day.
